Former Synagogue in Ehrstädt (Sinsheim)

Former Synagogue · Sinsheim, Germany

The synagogue in Ehrstädt, now a district of Sinsheim, was built in 1836 to a design executed by local master builder Franz Joseph Kistner, funded partly through a collection among Jewish communities of the Grand Duchy of Baden. As the Jewish community dwindled through emigration, it dissolved in 1912 and the synagogue building was sold; it was subsequently used as a barn and stable, which is likely why it escaped destruction during the 1938 pogrom. The city of Sinsheim later acquired the building, which was fully restored in 2004-05. Little of the original interior survives, and the space of the former Torah shrine niche is now only indicated within the modern renovation.
